message.content:
LeBron James is an American professional basketball player widely regarded as one of the greatest athletes in the history of the sport. Born on December 30, 1984, in Akron, Ohio, he rose to prominence as a high school phenom at St. Vincent‑St. Mary High School before being selected first overall in the 2003 NBA Draft by the Cleveland Cavaliers.

**Career Highlights**

| Team | Years | Achievements |
|------|-------|--------------|
| Cleveland Cavaliers | 2003–2010, 2014–2018 | NBA Finals appearances (2007, 2015, 2016), 2016 NBA Championship |
| Miami Heat | 2010–2014 | NBA Championships (2012, 2013) |
| Los Angeles Lakers | 2018–present | NBA Championship (2020) |

- **NBA MVP Awards:** 2009, 2010, 2012, 2013, 2016
- **All‑NBA First Team Selections:** 13 times
- **All‑Defensive First Team Selections:** 5 times
- **Olympic Gold Medals:** 2008 (Beijing), 2012 (London)

**Playing Style & Impact**

LeBron is known for his exceptional combination of size, athleticism, and basketball IQ. Standing 6'9" and weighing around 250 pounds, he can play virtually any position on the floor. His passing vision, court awareness, and ability to finish at the rim make him a dominant scorer and facilitator. Off the court, LeBron has been active in philanthropy, notably through the LeBron James Family Foundation, and has pursued ventures in media, entertainment, and business.

**Legacy**

LeBron James is often compared with other basketball legends such as Michael Jordan, Magic Johnson, and Kareem Abdul‑Jabbar. He has consistently demonstrated leadership, resilience, and excellence across multiple teams and eras, cementing his place among the all-time greats in the NBA.
